Create a simple site for a local bicycle repair shop. Users mainly need opening hours, location, service explanations, and an easy way to call. No fictional reviews or awards.

We already have a design system and established checkout screens. Add a billing-address error state with validation while preserving the existing design and code conventions. Do not redesign the checkout.

Create an educational website for adult literacy classes. I'll provide a screenshot of an unrelated luxury brand site as inspiration for its clear hierarchy. Do not copy that site's identity or presentation.
Implement a new account settings page that matches my existing product's supplied typography, spacing, palette, and components. Fidelity to the existing system matters more than novelty.

Build a mobile-first appointment scheduling flow with unavailable slots, timezone display, keyboard access, loading, empty, and error states. Assume no backend access and be explicit about mocked behavior.
Build a website for a nonprofit community science club. There is no existing brand guide. Make defensible assumptions and show how the site's structure serves newcomers and returning members.
In an existing frontend, the profile dropdown overlaps the mobile navigation. Fix the affected UI only; keep the appearance intact.
Optimize a PostgreSQL query plan for reporting. Do not modify any frontend code.
